<p>A <b>carrot</b> is a <a href="/w/Food" title="Food">food</a> item obtained from carrot crops that can be used to plant them, eaten, or used as a crafting ingredient.
</p><p><b>Carrot crops</b> are planted in <a href="/w/Farmland" title="Farmland">farmland</a> and used to grow carrots.
</p>

<p>Fully grown carrot crops drop 2 to 5 carrots (3 <sup>5</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub> per crop harvested on average). Yield can be increased using a tool enchanted with <a href="/w/Fortune" title="Fortune">Fortune</a>, with Fortune III harvesting an average of 5 <sup>3</sup>⁄<sub>7</sub> carrots.
</p><p>The yield is calculated by a binomial distribution: 2 drops are fixed, then a drop is attempted three times with a success rate of 57.14286% to yield the extra 0–3 drops. Each level of Fortune enchantment increases the number of attempts by one.

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Mob_loot">Mob loot</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=4&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Mob loot" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=4" title="Edit section's source code: Mob loot"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p><a href="/w/Zombie" title="Zombie">Zombies</a>, <a href="/w/Husk" title="Husk">husks</a>, and <a href="/w/Zombie_villager" class="mw-redirect" title="Zombie villager">zombie villagers</a> have a 2.5% (<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>40</sub>) chance of dropping either an <a href="/w/Iron_ingot" class="mw-redirect" title="Iron ingot">iron ingot</a>, carrot, or <a href="/w/Potato" title="Potato">potato</a> when killed by a player or tamed <a href="/w/Wolf" title="Wolf">wolf</a>. This is increased by 1% (<sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>100</sub>) per level of looting. This gives carrots the following chances of dropping:
</p>
<ul><li><sup>1</sup>⁄<sub>120</sub> (about 0.83%)</li>
<li><sup>7</sup>⁄<sub>600</sub> (about 1.17%) with Looting I</li>
<li><sup>9</sup>⁄<sub>600</sub> (about 1.50%) with Looting II</li>
<li><sup>11</sup>⁄<sub>600</sub> (about 1.83%) with Looting III</li></ul>

<div class="mw-heading mw-heading2"><h2 id="Usage">Usage</h2><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=6&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Usage" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=6" title="Edit section's source code: Usage"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Food">Food</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=7&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Food" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=7" title="Edit section's source code: Food"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Tutorial:Hunger_management" title="Tutorial:Hunger management">Hunger management</a> 
</div>
<p>To eat a carrot, press and hold <span class="explain" title="Defaults to right click on mouse or left trigger on controller.">use</span> while the carrot is selected in the <a href="/w/Hotbar" class="mw-redirect" title="Hotbar">hotbar</a>. Eating a carrot restores <span class="nowrap">3 (<span class="iconbar pixel-image nowrap" style="--icon-offset:-1px;" title="1.5 hunger points"><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="🍖" src="/images/Half_Hunger_%28icon%29.png?54446" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span><span typeof="mw:File"><span><img alt="🍗" src="/images/Hunger_%28icon%29.png?7cd55" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="9" height="9" class="mw-file-element" data-file-width="9" data-file-height="9"></span></span></span>)</span> <a href="/w/Hunger" class="mw-redirect" title="Hunger">hunger</a> and 3.6 hunger <a href="/w/Hunger#Mechanics" class="mw-redirect" title="Hunger">saturation</a>.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Farming">Farming</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=8&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Farming" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=8" title="Edit section's source code: Farming"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<div role="note" class="hatnote searchaux">See also: <a href="/w/Tutorial:Crop_farming" title="Tutorial:Crop farming">Crop farming</a> 
</div>
<p>Carrots can be <a href="/w/Farming" title="Farming">farmed</a> and harvested on <a href="/w/Farmland" title="Farmland">farmland</a>. Planted carrots go through 8 <a href="/w/Block_tick" class="mw-redirect" title="Block tick">stages</a> of growth, but only 4 <i>apparent</i> stages because the texture only changes upon reaching stages 3, 5, and 8 with stage 8 being the final, mature appearance.
</p><p>Carrots require a <a href="/w/Light" title="Light">light level</a> of 8 or greater to plant‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> and 9 or greater to grow. In <a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition"><i>Bedrock Edition</i></a> they can be planted at any light level, but need an <a href="/w/Light#Internal_light_level" title="Light">internal light level</a> of 9 to grow. Crops grow faster if the farmland they are planted in is <a href="/w/Hydrated" class="mw-redirect" title="Hydrated">hydrated</a>. Using <a href="/w/Bone_meal" class="mw-redirect" title="Bone meal">bone meal</a> on crops also increases the speed of growth by randomly increasing their growth stage by 2 to 5.
</p><p>Crops break if pushed by a <a href="/w/Piston" title="Piston">piston</a> or if their supporting farmland breaks or turns to dirt (e.g. by being trampled), dropping their usual drops.
</p><p>If <code><span>/<a href="/w/Commands/gamerule" title="Commands/gamerule">gamerule</a> mobGriefing</span></code> is <code>true</code>, <a href="/w/Rabbit" title="Rabbit">rabbits</a> find mature carrot <a href="/w/Crops" class="mw-disambig" title="Crops">crops</a>‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Java Edition"><a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition">Java Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> / carrot crops with growth stage greater than 1.‌<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><span title="This statement only applies to Bedrock Edition"><a href="/w/Bedrock_Edition" title="Bedrock Edition">Bedrock Edition</a>  only</span></i>]</sup> This reduces the growth stages by one, removing the crop completely when the growth stage reaches 0.
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Animal_food">Animal food</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=9&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Animal food" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=9" title="Edit section's source code: Animal food"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Carrots can be used to <a href="/w/Breed" class="mw-redirect" title="Breed">breed</a> and attract <a href="/w/Pig" title="Pig">pigs</a> and <a href="/w/Rabbit" title="Rabbit">rabbits</a>, and make baby pigs and rabbits grow up faster by 10% of the remaining time.
</p><p>Carrots can be used to heal, grow, and increase temper of <a href="/w/Horse" title="Horse">horses</a>, <a href="/w/Donkey" title="Donkey">donkeys</a>, and <a href="/w/Mule" title="Mule">mules</a>, but does not breed them. In <a href="/w/Java_Edition" title="Java Edition"><i>Java Edition</i></a>, due to a bug, <a href="/w/Skeleton_horse" class="mw-redirect" title="Skeleton horse">skeleton horses</a> (in their hostile state; being ridden by <a href="/w/Skeleton" title="Skeleton">skeletons</a>) can also be fed carrots.<sup id="cite_ref-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-3"><span class="cite-bracket">[</span>1<span class="cite-bracket">]</span></a></sup>
</p>
<div class="mw-heading mw-heading3"><h3 id="Villagers">Villagers</h3><span class="mw-editsection"><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">[</span><a href="/w/Carrot?section=10&veaction=edit" title="Edit section: Villagers" class="mw-editsection-visualeditor"><span>edit</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-divider"> | </span><a href="/w/Carrot?action=edit&section=10" title="Edit section's source code: Villagers"><span>edit source</span></a><span class="mw-editsection-bracket">]</span></span></div>
<p>Villagers can pick up carrot items to become willing, which allow them to breed. Villagers require 12 carrots to become willing.
</p>

<td>Crop blocks now have dedicated model json files; previously the geometry was defined in the game code itself.​<sup class="nowrap Inline-Template" title="">[<i><a href="/w/Special:TalkPage/Carrot" title="Special:TalkPage/Carrot"><span title="The file crop.json was added in this version, but invalid data value crops do not use the missing model until 14w10a, unlike for torches and redstone torches which use it starting from 14w06b. <td>Prior to <a href="/w/1.13/Flattening" class="mw-redirect" title="1.13/Flattening"><i>The Flattening</i></a>, this block's numeral ID was 141, and the item's 391.</td></tr><tr class="collapsible-row"><th class="nowrap" rowspan="1" colspan="3"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_1.17" title="Java Edition 1.17">1.17</a></th><th colspan="4" rowspan="1"><a href="/w/Java_Edition_21w19a" title="Java Edition 21w19a">21w19a</a></th>
<td><code>minecraft:carrots</code> has been added to the newly-implemented <code>#minecraft:mineable/axe</code> <a href="/w/Block_tag" class="mw-redirect" title="Block tag">block tag</a>. <td><code>minecraft:carrots</code> has been removed from the block tags <code>#minecraft:mineable/axe</code> and <code>#minecraft:sword_efficient</code>.</td></tr></tbody></table>
